reads.AORT: mixed — an idiosyncratic de-rate with rising absolute EBITDA and constructive targets, offset by two successive guidance cuts, an On-X recall and 3.3x leverage.
reads.BRBR: mixed — a real, consensus-confirmed EBITDA collapse offset by intact category demand, re-accelerating Q3 sales and an announced fiscal-2027 pricing lever.
reads.CNXC: mixed — near-record absolute EBITDA and FCF-positive self-funding sit against a crystallised impairment, 4.1x leverage and sharp forward-estimate cuts.
reads.EPAM: mixed — margins/ROIC/North-America softness and unanimous estimate cuts pull bearish, but rising absolute EBITDA, net cash and a compounding AI-native leg counter it.
reads.FUBO: mixed — scaled revenue and a contractual EBITDA step-up sit against deep cash burn, a zero-crossing earnings path, and opaque runway.
reads.IT: mixed — near-floor multiple and intact high-return subscription franchise against a genuinely stalled top line and shrinking new business.
reads.MVST: strongly-bearish — a stated going-concern doubt plus a ~$104M near-term maturity wall and reversing volume outweigh the FY25 margin inflection.
reads.NCNO: mixed — a genuine cash-generative EBITDA inflection and near-peer forward multiples offset by decelerating growth and unproven returns on capital.
reads.NFLX: mixed — a genuinely earned premium and long stated runway sit against a severe price drawdown and sharply negative forward revisions.
reads.SMPL: mixed — a self-funding, durably profitable franchise with a growing Quest core, offset by secular Atkins erosion, ongoing impairments and still-falling estimates.
reads.UBER: strongly-bullish — absolute EBITDA, ROIC and gross-bookings all inflecting up while the multiple sits at its own-history floor.
reads.V: strongly-bullish — a still-compounding, self-funding franchise (VAS +34%, RoC 30.3%) whose premium is largely earned by superior economics, though growth is moderating.
reads.VITL: mixed — an intact, growing brand and clean balance sheet against a 97% FY26 EBITDA reset whose margin recovery management itself defers to 2027.
reads.VRRM: strongly-bearish — a permanent >10%-of-revenue customer loss plus repeated guidance cuts and a segment impairment outweigh a growing but smaller Government book.
